focus: Q1 part 2: compiled routing order, surface hints, manifest freshness, route sync, and canary coverage
noveltyJustification: All five findings are new in this lineage because iteration 1 covered hub-level source files and not compiled routing or its canary corpus.
keyQuestions: Q1: Where is the surface order (opencode, obsidian, webflow) encoded, and where are sk-code-obsidian and sk-code-webflow treated as installed?

label: ORDER: Compiled sk-code precedence is copied from hub-router data. buildRoutingModel passes routerPolicy.tieBreak into bundleRules and copies that list into the compiled routing model; the current authored list puts quality, review, OpenCode, Obsidian, then Webflow.

ORDER: --surface-hint is a per-call reorder of a surface already present in the evaluated route. The hinted surface leads the surface targets, unknown or unmatched hints do nothing, and workflow modes keep their place.

PRESENCE: The sk-code canary fixture names Webflow and Obsidian packet ids in expected bundles and hint cases. Its harness compiles those cases against the current hub registry, router, and skill text, so the canary corpus is anchored to the operator repository surface set.

PRESENCE: The surface-hint test asserts Webflow and Obsidian behavior for sk-code, while its no-surface-packet case uses sk-doc and mcp-tooling. These inspected cases do not establish what happens to sk-code when the two example packets are deleted.

OK: The promoted sk-code activation manifest stores selected policy hash, generation, and serving authority, not the surface tie-break. Parent freshness checking rereads SKILL.md, hub-router.json, and mode-registry.json, recompiles at the selected generation, then compares generation and effectivePolicyHash. The serving-closure sync separately fingerprints its manifest and enumerated files.
